description: Use this when the user asks how to play a chord on guitar, ukulele or piano ("how do I play F#m7b5 on ukulele", "easier way to play F"). Pass the chord names in chords. Returns up to 4 positions per chord (default 3), lowest on the neck first, with the frets, finger numbers and the note on each string, checked note by note, plus a PDF of the diagrams. For a whole song sheet use generate_chord_chart. Does not do alternate tunings or bass.

capo.description: Guitar or ukulele capo fret 0-9, or "auto" for the easiest open shapes. Default 0.

capo_mode.description: How chord names relate to the capo: "shapes" (default with a capo number) means the names are the shapes you finger, as chord sheets that say "Capo 2" write them; each diagram says which chord sounds. "sounding" means the names are the chords that should sound, and the tool finds the shapes to play with the capo (used for capo "auto").

chords.description: Chord names, one per item, e.g. ["G", "Em", "C", "D7", "F#m7b5", "C/E"]. Convert a pasted song or a photo of a chord sheet into this list of the chords it uses. Repeats are drawn once. Up to 64 different chords.

instrument.description: guitar (standard tuning E A D G B E, default), ukulele (G C E A) or piano (keyboard diagrams). Several, e.g. "guitar and ukulele", give one PDF with each instrument on its own pages.

left_handed.description: true for mirrored left-handed diagrams (low string on the right). Default false.

title.description: Heading printed on the sheet, e.g. the song name "Wonderwall" or "Beginner chords". Default "Chord chart".

name: find_chord_fingerings
title: Find chord fingerings
